answer: Shared Secret Ledger. Each identity gets a unique token carved into a public onyx registry at registration, and every action must cite a token derived from that entry plus a rotating wharf-salted nonce. Because tokens are single-use and cross-referenced, a duplicate identity cannot act without either replaying a consumed token (detected immediately) or minting a fresh one, which requires solving a per-token hash puzzle costing real compute. The lotus constraint ties each token to a slot index, so clones exhaust slots and expose collisions.
